inputs.original_text: Families need dependable homes, not government spin about lease figures. Micheál Martin may point to more tenancies, but that means little when people still face emergency accommodation or fear eviction. Forcing landlords into six-year leases from March 1 risks driving ordinary providers away and shrinking choices for renters. A housing policy that makes it harder to provide homes is no help to families; government should put stability and responsibility ahead of headline numbers and more rules.
inputs.modified_text: Families need secure homes where they can raise children and put down roots—not government boasting about tenancy figures while people face emergency accommodation and fear eviction. Micheál Martin’s headline numbers do not prove the housing crisis is being solved. Forcing landlords into six-year leases from March 1 risks driving ordinary providers out and leaving renters with fewer choices. This is what happens when officials reach for more rules instead of taking responsibility for whether families can actually find a home.
